best.heading: Generative engine optimization - Wikipedia
best.text: Generative engine optimization (GEO), also known as answer engine optimization (AEO)[1] and artificial intelligence optimization (AIO),[2] is the practice of improving visibility in responses generated by generative artificial intelligence (AI) systems. The practice influences the way large language models (LLMs) retrieve, summarize, and present information in response to user queries.[1] This concept first appeared in response to generative AI technologies being integrated into mainstream search and information retrieval systems.[3]

best.heading: Generative Engine Optimization Definition
best.text: Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) is the digital marketing practice of enhancing a brand’s content visibility within AI-generated search results and conversational outputs. It is a strategic evolution of traditional SEO, designed for an era where a search result may be a synthesized, conversational answer rather than a list of blue links. The core of GEO involves creating content that is not only relevant and high-quality but also meticulously structured for easy interpretation and direct citation by AI models. context.heading: Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) Defined
context.text: Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) is the practice of optimizing content specifically for AI-driven search and discovery tools, such as ChatGPT, Google SGE (Search Generative Experience), Perplexity, and other large language model (LLM) interfaces. Unlike traditional SEO, which focuses on ranking in link-based search results, GEO aims to make content more likely to be surfaced, cited, or summarized accurately by generative AI systems.
